terms.definition: An element in Group 17 — a reactive nonmetal with seven valence electrons, one short of a full shell.
terms.function: Reacts eagerly by grabbing one extra electron to fill its outer shell, becoming a -1 ion.
terms.whereItIs: Group 17 — the second-to-last column of the periodic table.
terms.whyItMatters: Halogens build the salts, disinfectants, and plastics of everyday life.

terms.definition: The electrons in an atom's outermost shell; halogens have seven.
terms.function: Determines bonding — with seven, a halogen needs just one more to reach a full, stable shell.
terms.whereItIs: The seven teal electrons on the atom model's outer ring.
terms.whyItMatters: That one missing electron makes halogens among the most reactive nonmetals.

terms.definition: A chlorine atom that has gained one electron, giving it a -1 charge and a full outer shell.
terms.function: Forms when a halogen grabs an electron; pairs with positive ions to build salts.
terms.whereItIs: The ion model beside the samples in the electron-grab layer.
terms.whyItMatters: Chloride ions in salt keep your body's fluids balanced.

terms.definition: The second-to-last column of the periodic table, home to the halogens.
terms.function: Stacks the seven-valence-electron nonmetal family together.
terms.whereItIs: The glowing second-to-last column in the model's table section.
terms.whyItMatters: Every element in this column shares the same grab-an-electron personality.
